bihar_raw_news.title: "Manufacture here": Bihar CM urges entrepreneurs to boost local production - ANI News
bihar_raw_news.content: "Manufacture here": Bihar CM urges entrepreneurs to boost local production ANI | Updated: Oct 08, 2026 19:38 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], October 8 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday said the state government has introduced the Bihar Purchase Preference Policy to promote manufacturing in the state and encourage entrepreneurs to produce goods locally. Choudhary was speaking at an orientation programme on the 'Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana' organised by the Industries Department at Bapu Sabhaghar in Patna. On the occasion, the instalment amount was transferred to the accounts of more than 7,000 beneficiaries, and the Bihar MSME Policy-2026 was launched. Explaining the government's approach under the Purchase Preference Policy, Choudhary said a system has been put in place through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) portal and that a system for auctions has also been introduced. The CM said, “We introduced Bihar Purchase Preference Policy. A system has been put in place through GeM (Government e Marketplace) portal. Upload your product there. We now have a system for auctions too. But under the Bihar Purchase Preference Policy, be it purchasing steel or garments or any raw material, the Govt has decided to purchase only those products whose 25%-40% of the manufacturing has been done in Bihar. So, manufacture here.” Earlier, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary inspected the Ankur Biochem Private Limited ethanol plant, currently under construction in the Chakai block of Jamui district. During the inspection, officials briefed the Chief Minister about the plant's construction work and the project's progress. Officials stated that production at the plant would commence by March 2027. Following the inspection, a review meeting was held at the ethanol plant premises, chaired by the Chief Minister, Samrat Chaudhary. According to a press release, during the meeting, Jamui District Magistrate Naveen gave a presentation providing detailed information about the Ankur Biochem Private Limited ethanol plant, noting that this project is one of Asia's largest grain-based ethanol plants. It is being developed on a 105-acre site. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: CM Choudhary sets target of 1 Crore entrepreneurs, pushes Bihar -made products in ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Patna: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary during the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Sabha event, organised to mark 25 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi in public service, in Patna on Wednesday, October 07, 2026. (Photo: IANS/X/@samrat4bjp) India 8th October 2026 Patna, October 8 (IANS) Bihar Chief Minister, Samrat Choudhary, has announced a series of measures to promote entrepreneurship, local manufacturing and employment in the state, saying the government aims to create employment opportunities for one crore people by 2030 and expand the role of local entrepreneurs in the economy. Choudhary made the announcements on Thursday while addressing an orientation programme for beneficiaries of the Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana at Patna's Bapu Sabhagar. During the event, the government also transferred the first or subsequent instalments of financial assistance to around 7,000 beneficiaries. CM Choudhary said the government has introduced a purchase-preference mechanism under which products manufactured in Bihar and meeting prescribed quality standards will receive priority in government procurement. He said the objective was to encourage entrepreneurs to establish production facilities within the state rather than manufacture products elsewhere and sell them in Bihar. For instance, if an entrepreneur can manufacture bicycles or other goods in Bihar, the government wants production to take place within the state. The policy is intended to create a market for local industries through government procurement. CM Choudhary has also said that the government would purchase a share of qualifying products manufactured by industries established in Bihar. Recent reports have put that assured share at 25 per cent for eligible products meeting prescribed standards. The Chief Minister also highlighted changes intended to increase the participation of Bihar-based entrepreneurs in government contracts. According to him, for government tenders valued at up to Rs 50 crore, a Bihar-based entrepreneur who ranks L2, L3, or L4 could be considered for the contract if willing to execute the work at the L1 rate. The stated objective is to provide greater opportunities to local entrepreneurs in government projects. CM Choudhary said the government is preparing around 45,000 new entrepreneurs under its entrepreneurship initiatives, while approximately 7,000 beneficiaries received their first or subsequent instalments during the programme. Around Rs 3,500 crore has been earmarked for the initiative, according to the government. The Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana provides eligible beneficiaries with financial assistance of up to Rs 10 lakh for setting up enterprises. Under the scheme, up to Rs 5 lakh is provided as a grant or subsidy and up to Rs 5 lakh as a loan, subject to the applicable scheme category and conditions. The beneficiaries include people from the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, Extremely Backward Classes, women, youth and minority communities. The official Udyami portal lists separate components of the scheme for these categories. CM Choudhary said entrepreneurship and the expansion of MSMEs would be central to the government's efforts to generate employment within Bihar. bihar_raw_news.content: SHARE A Bihar court has held former Rohtas Superintendent of Police Raushan Kumar guilty of contempt for wilfully failing to comply with judicial directions, imposing a symbolic fine of Re 1 and ordering that the conviction be entered into his service record. In an order dated September 29, 2026, District and Additional Sessions Judge-IV Anil Kumar directed the Rohtas District Magistrate to deduct the fine amount directly from the officer’s salary within 15 days and deposit it in the court treasury. Kumar, who currently serves as Senior Superintendent of Police in Saran, faced the penal action after repeatedly ignoring court directives and formal notices issued in connection with a trial. Training of civil servants requires overhaul Expressing serious concern over an attitude where subordinate judicial forums are treated as inferior, the court observed that such an approach runs counter to the healthy functioning of a democratic setup. Additional Sessions Judge Anil Kumar noted that the training curricula for Indian Administrative Service and Indian Police Service officers suffer from deep shortcomings and must be reformed to emphasize institutional accountability and deference to judicial mandates. The court directed that a copy of the ruling be forwarded to the Union Ministry of Personnel and Training, pointing out that administrative indifference to court summons is not limited to Bihar and citing a similar instance in Namakkal, Tamil Nadu, where a district magistrate allegedly failed to answer court notices. Disregard of directives during kidnapping trial The contempt proceedings originated from Sessions Trial Case No. 95/2023, wherein the trial court convicted 10 persons under Section 364-A of the Indian Penal Code for a kidnapping involving an alleged ransom demand of Rs 1.50 crore. Despite the victim and his informant son turning hostile during the proceedings after reportedly receiving Rs 20 lakh, the court decided the case on available evidence. It subsequently ordered the then Rohtas police chief to obtain fresh criminal antecedent reports of the convicts, register an FIR against the victim for alleged perjury, and examine the victim’s alleged ties to narcotics trade and gambling activities linked to his son. The required antecedent report was submitted nearly a month late, merely reproducing older case diary entries instead of providing fresh information. Failure to respond to show-cause notices Following the delay, the court issued a show-cause notice to the officer in July 2026, which went unanswered. Communications sent on July 16 to the Bihar Director General of Police and the Chief Secretary seeking departmental action and an action-taken report also drew no response. The court formally initiated contempt proceedings under Section 384 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita on August 17, 2026. While the officer later argued through counsel that the initial orders were never received, the court dismissed the defense upon confirming delivery to the Rohtas SP office. The court criticized the officer for avoiding personal appearance to lead evidence and attempting to influence the case through an eminent person. bihar_raw_news.title: US conducts 'SIR'-like voter verification: How millions of records are being reviewed to ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Home News Reports US conducts 'SIR'-like voter verification: How millions of records are being reviewed to identify... News Reports OpIndia Explains Updated: 8 October, 2026 US conducts ‘SIR’-like voter verification: How millions of records are being reviewed to identify noncitizen voters The US has launched a sweeping voter-roll scrutiny through ICE’s Homeland Security Investigations, analysing tens of millions of records and pursuing cases involving suspected noncitizen registration and voting. The exercise mirrors the broader principle behind India’s SIR: periodically verifying electoral rolls to identify ineligible entries and protect the integrity of elections. 8 October, 2026 Jinit Jain US is conducting its 'SIR' weeks after President Donald Trump praised India's CEC Gyanesh Kumar Facebook X Telegram Email WhatsApp For months, India’s Opposition has attempted to turn the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls into a political controversy. Opposition parties have repeatedly alleged that the exercise could exclude genuine voters and have sought to portray voter-roll verification as an attack on democracy. But an interesting development in the United States offers a rather different perspective. The United States government has launched an extensive operation to scrutinise voter-registration records, investigate suspected illegal registrations and identify cases involving people who may not have been eligible to vote. The exercise is being driven in significant part by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the investigative arm of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The scale of the operation is striking. According to internal documents reviewed by CNN, HSI described its undertaking as a phased national initiative involving voter-roll acquisition, data analysis, investigative leads and field investigations. Investigators had ingested 50.6 million records from a Justice Department dataset and another 48.4 million records obtained from what officials described as independent sources. In other words, the world’s most powerful democracy is not treating voter rolls as untouchable documents that cannot be scrutinised. It is doing precisely the opposite: collecting data, comparing records, identifying anomalies and investigating cases where officials believe electoral laws may have been violated. What exactly is ICE doing? It is important to understand that ICE itself is a large federal law-enforcement agency, while Homeland Security Investigations is one of its investigative components. HSI normally deals with serious transnational crimes such as human trafficking, drug smuggling, organised crime, financial crimes and document fraud. Its involvement in election-related investigations represents a significant deployment of federal investigative resources. It was reported in September that HSI had launched what internal guidance described as a “coordinated criminal voter fraud surge initiative.” The operation involved pursuing investigative leads, conducting field interviews and supporting prosecutorial review. Offices in nine states were assigned investigative leads, including Washington, Wisconsin, Missouri, Georgia, California, Pennsylvania, Nevada, New York and Connecticut. The operation was not limited to checking whether somebody’s name appeared on a voter list. Investigators were examining voter-registration data and following leads that could potentially result in criminal investigations. bihar_raw_news.title: Supreme Court Allows State Appeal, Dismisses Teacher's Reinstatement Due to Invalid ... - Lawtext
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Judgement Scroll Down To Discover Supreme Court Supreme Court Allows State Appeal, Dismisses Teacher's Reinstatement Due to Invalid Qualification. The respondent was not eligible for appointment as he lacked a qualification recognized by the NCTE as mandated by the Bihar Panchayat Elementary Teacher (Employment and Service Conditions) Rules, 2006. Admin 2026-10-08 18:08:50 21 Share This Article: Font size: Print Case Note & Summary This case involved a civil appeal by the State of Bihar against a Division Bench order of the Patna High Court that reinstated the respondent, as a Trained Block Teacher. The respondent had been appointed in 2007 based on a Senior Teacher Training Certificate issued by Dr. B. C. Roy College of Education, which was later found to be from an unrecognized institution. The State terminated his services in 2015, leading to a series of legal challenges. The District Teacher Appellate Authority initially set aside the termination, but this was reversed by the State Appellate Authority, which cited previous judgments regarding the college's lack of recognition. The respondent's appeal to the High Court resulted in a favorable ruling, which the State contested in the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court analyzed the eligibility criteria under the 2006 Rules and concluded that the respondent did not possess a valid qualification as required by the NCTE Act, which had come into effect prior to his appointment. The court found that the Division Bench had erred in its interpretation of the NCTE Act's applicability and ultimately allowed the State's appeal, dismissing the respondent's reinstatement. Headnote A) Administrative Law - Eligibility for Public Office - Requirement of Recognized Qualification - Bihar Panchayat Elementary Teacher (Employment and Service Conditions) Rules, 2006, Rule 8 - The respondent was appointed as a Trained Block Teacher without holding a qualification recognized by the NCTE, which was mandatory under the 2006 Rules. The court held that the Division Bench erred in applying the NCTE Act prospectively, emphasizing that eligibility must be assessed at the time of appointment. Thus, the appeal was allowed, and the order of reinstatement was set aside (Paras 4-4.2). bihar_raw_news.title: Vertical Road Construction: Economic Challenges Ahead, Warns Vertis Infrastructure Trust, ETInfra
bihar_raw_news.content: Roads and Highways 5 min read Parallel highway construction by different agencies can challenge project economics: Vertis Infrastructure Trust’s Zafar Khan Vertis Infrastructure Trust's Joint CEO Zafar Khan said there is a need for coordination between state and central authorities on road network development in the country so that there is no unnecessary wastage of resources. Dev Kachari ETInfra Published On Oct 8, 2026 at 06:13 PM IST Select ETInfra as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook “UP is continuously building new highways without any consideration of the national highway. So you have three national highway types of road parallel to each other. Now there is no requirement why the state government is pushing money for building six lane highways and the traffic is just 10,000 PCU ( Passenger Car Unit).” said Khan. NEW DELHI: The country over the past one decade has seen expeditious development of national highways and expressways, which have resulted in the road infrastructure becoming one of the promising sectors for investment as well as asset monetisation. However, the development undertaken by various authorities, in the central and state governments, can potentially give rise to network development risk. Advt Speaking to ETInfra , Zafar Khan, Executive Director and Joint Chief Executive Officer of Vertis Infrastructure Trust, highlighted that development of parallel roads by different executing authorities can challenge the economic feasibility of road infrastructure being developed in the country. “Bihar, UP (Uttar Pradesh), these are the states where new highways are getting constructed and there is no large-level coordination between the state authority and the central authority in terms of planning these highways,” said Khan, who also serves as President of the Highways Investor Association. In UP, over the last few years, several expressway projects have been executed by Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA), which are in addition to existing national highways in the state. “UP is continuously building new highways without any consideration of the national highway. So you have three national highway types of road parallel to each other. Now there is no requirement why the state government is pushing money for building six lane highways and the traffic is just 10,000 PCU ( Passenger Car Unit).” said Khan. “But from the economical parameters and the feasibility of highways and more investment, having parallel highways is unnecessary wastage of capital expenditure….,” added Khan. For Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) such as Vertis, which manages operational road and highway assets, the development of highways and road infrastructure parallel (also referred to as competing road) to the assets managed by them has the potential to cause traffic diversion and revenue loss. Advt Vertis is a diversified transportation infrastructure platform managing 8,428 lane kilometres of highway assets across nine states, including Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) as well Toll-Operate-Transfer (TOT) road portfolio with assets under management exceeding ₹27,000 crore. bihar_raw_news.title: Gadkari Announces Rs. 5 tn Road Projects for Bihar - RAHSTA Expo
bihar_raw_news.content: Gadkari Announces Rs. 5 tn Road Projects for Bihar Infrastructure Transport Oct 08 2026 Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari has said road infrastructure projects worth around Rs. 3.88 tn are planned in Bihar, with the Centre targeting completion of road works worth nearly Rs. 5 tn in the state by the end of the current term. He made the announcement at the Rising Bihar Investor Summit 2026 in Patna. Projects covering around 2,910 km and costing nearly Rs. 330 bn have been completed or incurred expenditure in Bihar, while work is under way on another 1,878 km involving about Rs. 651 bn. Proposed projects account for an estimated investment of nearly Rs. 3.25 tn. The national highway network in the state has expanded from around 4,615 km in 2014 to nearly 6,500 km. Among the major projects is the 440-km Ram-Janki Marg, estimated to cost Rs. 54.4 bn, with 27 per cent of work completed and completion targeted for November 2028. Projects worth around Rs. 220 bn are also being undertaken along a corridor connected with sites associated with Lord Buddha, with about 90 per cent of work completed. The proposed Gorakhpur-Siliguri High-Speed Corridor will cover around 526 km, including nearly 410 km in Bihar, and is estimated to cost Rs. 720 bn. Bihar’s proposed investment is approximately Rs. 520 bn. Other projects include the 400-km Patna-Purnea Greenfield Expressway, the 218-km Buxar-Bhagalpur High-Speed Corridor costing Rs. 100 bn, and the 13.4-km Anisabad-Didarganj project estimated at Rs. 85 bn. The Varanasi-Ranchi-Kolkata Corridor, costing around Rs. 320 bn, is about 35 per cent complete, while the proposed 550-km Raxaul-Haldia Corridor is estimated at Rs. 452 bn, with around Rs. 260 bn proposed for Bihar. Gadkari also highlighted the 162-km Patna Ring Road, estimated at Rs. 102 bn, saying the wider network could reduce travel and logistics costs, improve market access and support investment, industry and employment. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Forest Department Takes Responsibility for Highway Clearance - RAHSTA Expo
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Forest Department Takes Responsibility for Highway Clearance Infrastructure Transport Oct 08 2026 Bihar’s forest department has agreed to obtain forest clearance and oversee execution of a highway widening project on forest land, despite its regulatory role in assessing such applications. The arrangement was formalised through a memorandum of understanding signed with the state’s Road Construction Department (RCD) on September 26. The agreement covers the widening and strengthening of a 10.5-kilometre section of National Highway 333 through Gangata forest in Munger district. The existing single-lane road is to be converted into a two-lane carriageway, with the project intended to improve connectivity, road safety and traffic movement. The project requires 2.1 hectares of forest land from Bhimband Wildlife Sanctuary. An application for forest clearance was submitted in April 2023 and one for wildlife clearance in February 2024, but the Parivesh single-window portal records the application status as pending at the state level. The MoU requires the forest department to assist with processing forest diversion approvals, facilitate access to the required land and support the expedited handling of related statutory permissions. It also gives the department execution responsibility, including contractual administration during the defect-liability period, while assigning the Divisional Forest Officer, Munger, responsibility for processing bills, making payments and maintaining financial records. The same officer is responsible under the applicable process for the preliminary field assessment of forest clearance applications within the jurisdiction. The department’s head of forest force, Arvinder Singh, has said the MoU is being withdrawn after concerns were raised about the potential conflict between its regulatory and project-delivery roles. The RCD will retain responsibility for the sanctioned estimate, bidding documents, tendering and award of work. It will also deploy engineering staff to supervise construction, check quality, record measurements and scrutinise bills, while forest personnel will work alongside them. The project runs between kilometre 28.340 and kilometre 38.840, and its revised cost is Rs. 510 mn. Tags: Bihar forest department NH 333 forest clearance

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar to Open Labour Facilitation Centres for Migrants in Tamil Nadu - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar to Open Labour Facilitation Centres for Migrants in Tamil Nadu Breaking News Bihar to Open Labour Facilitation Centres for Migrants in Tamil Nadu By Urban Acres October 8, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp The Bihar government will set up Labour Service Facilitation Centres in Chennai, Coimbatore and Tiruppur within the next two months to help migrant workers access grievance redressal, welfare schemes, workplace rights and social security support, according to a report by the Times of India. The centres, called Shram Seva Suvidha Kendra, are being established by Bihar’s Labour Resource and Migrant Workers Welfare department as the state seeks to build a database of residents who leave for employment in other states and countries. K Senthil Kumar, additional chief secretary of the department, said the initiative was intended to understand the movement and livelihood conditions of migrant workers and support them through government programmes. “We have more than 3 crore Biharis going out to work interstate and internationally across various industries. So, the idea of the centre is to create a database on how many workers leave the state for work to help them with their livelihoods in every possible way,” Kumar was quoted as saying. The department plans to provide support on language and cultural orientation, workplace-related problems, social security schemes, education for workers’ children, health insurance, accident compensation and death compensation. The centres will also help workers access government schemes for which they may be eligible. Tamil Nadu has been identified as one of the main locations for the initiative because of the concentration of workers from Bihar in its industrial and employment hubs. The department has selected Chennai, Coimbatore and Tiruppur, which it described as hotspots for migrant workers. Kumar said close to 2-3 lakh Biharis were working in Tiruppur. The proposed centres are part of a wider plan to establish 12 such facilities across India. The Bihar department has already begun the initiative in Karnataka and has conducted or initiated an extensive survey across 12 states, including Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Delhi-NCR, Kerala, Punjab and Maharashtra. The survey is intended to record workers’ socio-economic conditions and identify the government schemes most suitable for them. The move places a state government’s migrant-worker administration alongside the labour systems of the destination states. For workers, the centres are expected to provide a local point of contact in cities where language differences, unfamiliarity with public services and distance from their home administration can make it difficult to report workplace problems or claim benefits. The announcement also reflects the scale of interstate labour movement from Bihar. The department said it was working to create more employment opportunities within the state, including through the proposed establishment of a cement factory and a sugar factory. The immediate plan in Tamil Nadu, however, is focused on documentation, facilitation and welfare access for workers already living and working there. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi. The four-day event, which began yesterday, showcases India’s remarkable progress in telecommunications, digital connectivity and technological innovation. The theme of IMC 2026 is ‘Scale Without Boundaries’, reflecting India’s growing capabilities in digital innovation, next-generation connectivity and technology-led growth. Inaugurating the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress, PM Modi said the platform has witnessed the evolution of India’s telecom sector and digital connectivity over the years. He said the platform has emerged as a showcase of India’s progress and aspirations. The Prime Minister said 5G connectivity has reached every district of the country. He said the government is now working to connect around 25 crore students through various digital and online education platforms. Prime Minister Modi said digital connectivity has powered education, healthcare and government services. national_raw_news.title: 7 hours ago | National 480 FM Nirmala Sitharaman chairs 57th GST Council meeting in New Delhi
national_raw_news.content: The 57th GST Council meeting is underway at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman is chairing the meeting. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Karnataka Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, and Finance Ministers of States and Union Territories are also attending the meeting. The GST Council meeting will discuss policy reforms to resolve GST disputes and improve the flow of input tax credit, with the aim of reducing the time and cost of compliance. Sources in the Finance Ministry said that the government will propose a five-pronged plan for the next set of reforms to the Goods and Services Tax (GST) system. These reforms are aimed at automating and easing many of the current administrative bottlenecks in the GST system and reducing the compliance burden, especially for small businesses. The five-pronged proposal covers process reforms, structural reforms, ease of living and doing business, exports of services, and e-commerce. Some of the key changes proposed involve automatic invoice matching between buyers and sellers, reducing paperwork around claiming input tax credits (ITC), reducing the number of times small taxpayers have to file returns, and removing multi-state registrations for small businesses. The last, 56th meeting of the GST Council was held in September last year. During the meeting, the Council approved rate rationalisation with a focus on the common man, labour-intensive industries, farmers and agriculture, health, and key drivers of the economy.
